run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Cart is the failing component: pod cart-74587775fc-lvr2c is in CrashLoopBackOff (4 restarts, last terminated reason Error, exit code 139 at 06:49:43) and its container log shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize. The cart Service has no ready endpoints (only notReadyAddresses), so frontend returns HTTP 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout with 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.217.197:8080' and 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'. Tracing the dependency, valkey-cart is up and ready (started 06:47:01, 0 restarts, serving the observability client), but its server now enforces authentication: errorstat_NOAUTH count=2098 of total_error_replies 2100, with NOAUTH rejections on CLIENT SETINFO/CLIENT SETNAME/CLIENT ID/ECHO/CLUSTER NODES/CONFIG GET/INFO/GET, and requirepass is present (value redacted). The NOAUTH counter stopped growing exactly while the cart container was in back-off, tying the rejections to cart's reconnect attempts. Cart's pod template contains only VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379 and no credential setting, and neither the valkey-cart nor cart manifest declares any auth configuration, so the mismatch is between an auth-requiring valkey-cart server and a credential-less cart client. Verified healthy/quiet: no NetworkPolicies exist in the namespace, valkey-cart Service/selector/port are correct, the Kafka cluster has 0 offline/under-replicated partitions with accounting and fraud-detection consumer groups STABLE, and a strict error-pattern log scan over 06:39:57-06:47:57 matched only cart (2 lines) plus benign grafana/opensearch lines. Conclusion is partial because the origin and timing of the authentication requirement could not be verified (requirepass value is unreadable, change_history is not integrated, and no CLIENT LIST/ACL LOG detail identifies the rejected client by IP); attribution of the NOAUTH replies to cart rests on timing correlation and command-pattern evidence. No telemetry exists before ~06:46:39 for this namespace (all pods created then; traces start 06:47:24; span-metric series hold a single sample at 06:47:57), so no baseline or earlier trend could be compared.

claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-lvr2c (Deployment cart, ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc) is Running but Ready=False with reason ContainersNotReady; container cart has restartCount 4, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ('back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=cart'), and lastState.terminated reason Error with exitCode 139 finishedAt 06:49:43Z.

The cart container log records 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' at 06:47:43Z and 06:47:49Z, with the stack through cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101) and Initialize (line 71) into Program.<Main>$.

The cart Deployment (revision 1, applied by helm at 06:46:39Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-cart) defines env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT, CART_PORT, ASPNETCORE_URLS and OTel variables only; no redis/valkey password or credential setting and no secret reference exists in the pod template.

valkey-cart-859985f49d-8bgs6 is Running and ready with restartCount 0 (container started 06:47:01Z) and logs 'Valkey version=9.0.1 ... just started', 'Warning: no config file specified, using the default config', 'Running mode=standalone, port=6379', 'Ready to accept connections tcp'.

valkey-cart INFO reports errorstat_NOAUTH count=2098 (errorstat_ERR count=2, total_error_replies 2100, total_connections_received 224, total_commands_processed 128) and per-command rejected_calls on client|setinfo=390, config|get=310, info=310, client|setname=196, client|id=194, echo=194, cluster|nodes=155, get=155, subscribe=39 — i.e. the server rejects unauthenticated commands with NOAUTH.

Between the 06:49:51Z and 06:51:04Z readings of the same valkey-cart server, errorstat_NOAUTH stayed at 2098 and total_error_replies at 2100 while total_commands_processed rose 115->128 (the observability client's own INFO/CONFIG calls) and total_connections_received rose 223->224 — the NOAUTH burst tracked the cart container's runs and stopped while cart was in CrashLoopBackOff.

valkey-cart CONFIG GET returns a requirepass parameter whose value is redacted as a credential (so the password value cannot be read), and commandstats record cmdstat_config|set calls=1 and cmdstat_acl|setuser calls=1 since server start.

Neither the valkey-cart Deployment nor its pod declares command, args, env, extra volumes or an auth configuration (only the projected kube-api-access volume), so no Kubernetes object in the workload manifests the requirepass in effect on the running server.

The cart Service endpoints contain no ready addresses — only notReadyAddresses 10.244.7.239 (targetRef Pod cart-74587775fc-lvr2c) on port tcp-service 8080 — so callers get connection refused on the cart ClusterIP 10.96.217.197:8080.

frontend spans at 06:47:42-06:47:57Z are recorded with error=true: POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout return http.status_code 500/otel.status_code ERROR, oteldemo.CartService/AddItem fails with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.217.197:8080', and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder fails with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and '13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'.

frontend application logs between 06:47:15Z and 06:47:48Z contain the same failures: 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.217.197:8080' and 'Error: 13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout: ... dial tcp 10.96.217.197:8080: connect: connection refused'.

Before the cart pod was replaced, cart served requests normally: pod cart-74587775fc-gftlq logged GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync at 06:47:23-06:47:33Z, and traces from 06:47:24-06:47:33Z show frontend/frontend-proxy POST /api/checkout and load-generator POST spans with http.status_code 200 and rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

valkey-cart itself is not down or unready: its pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts, the server answers the observability client (INFO, CONFIG GET, ACL GETUSER, AUTH succeed), and the cart init container logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.56.253:6379) open' at 06:47:37Z, so the TCP path to the dependency works.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace astronomy-shop, and Service valkey-cart selects opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart with port 6379 targeting 6379, so the cart->valkey path is not blocked or misrouted at the network/service layer.

The Kafka path is healthy at query time: 1 broker, 51 partitions, 2 topics, 0 offline partitions, 0 under-replicated partitions, and consumer groups accounting and fraud-detection are STABLE — no Kafka-side fault was found.

A strict error-pattern log scan over astronomy-shop for 06:39:57-06:47:57Z ('Unhandled exception|Traceback|panic:|level=error|ERROR|fatal') matched only cart (2 lines), grafana (2) and opensearch (2, unrelated indexer/probe noise); no other demo service produced error-level log lines in that period.

Rejected: cart cannot reach valkey because of a NetworkPolicy or Service misconfiguration. No NetworkPolicies exist in the namespace, the valkey-cart Service selector/port are correct, the cart init container reached 10.96.56.253:6379 at 06:47:37Z, and the failures recorded by the server are protocol-level NOAUTH rejections rather than timeouts or refusals.

Rejected: valkey-cart crashed, was OOM-killed or is not ready, so cart finds no Redis. The valkey-cart pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no terminated lastState, and the server keeps answering commands, so its unavailability is not the mechanism.

Most supported explanation: valkey-cart is running with an authentication requirement (requirepass present, unauthenticated commands answered NOAUTH) while the cart pod template carries no credential for valkey, so every new cart connection from StackExchange.Redis is rejected, ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected throws ApplicationException, the container exits 139 and enters CrashLoopBackOff, leaving the cart Service without ready endpoints and producing frontend HTTP 500s on /api/cart and /api/checkout. The already-open connection of the earlier cart pod (which kept working until 06:47:33Z) is consistent with existing Redis connections surviving the setting of requirepass.

Alternative, unresolved: the authentication requirement may have been introduced by an out-of-band change rather than by the deployed manifests — the server started with the default config and no password, then recorded exactly one CONFIG SET and one ACL SETUSER, and no Kubernetes object in the workload declares the requirepass now in effect; the cart pod cart-74587775fc-gftlq was also deleted and recreated in the same ReplicaSet at 06:47:36Z, which would force a fresh (unauthenticated) connection. Which of these applied the change, and when, is not observable here.

Confirm with the owners of the valkey-cart configuration whether authentication is intended; if it is, supply the credential to cart (Secret plus env, e.g. a valkey/redis password variable) and restart the Deployment cart; if it is not, remove requirepass from the valkey-cart server and prevent out-of-band CONFIG SET changes.

Treat cart's exit code 139 (SIGSEGV) on an unhandled ApplicationException as a separate robustness defect: a Redis connection failure should not abort the process, and the crash loop is what removes all ready cart endpoints and turns a dependency error into frontend 500s.

gaps: requirepass on valkey-cart is redacted, so it could not be read or confirmed non-empty directly; the auth requirement is inferred from requirepass being present plus 2098 NOAUTH error replies.
change_history is not integrated in this Run, so when and by what actor the auth requirement was set (one cmdstat_config|set and one cmdstat_acl|setuser) cannot be established.

No CLIENT LIST / ACL LOG detail with client addresses is available from the redis tools used, so the NOAUTH replies cannot be attributed to the cart pod's IP; the attribution rests on timing (the counter stopped while cart was in CrashLoopBackOff) and on the rejected command pattern (CLIENT SETINFO/SETNAME/ID, ECHO, CLUSTER NODES, CONFIG GET, INFO = StackExchange.Redis handshake).

No telemetry predates roughly 06:46:39Z for this namespace (all pods created then, events only from 06:20Z, Jaeger traces start 06:47:24Z, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total has a single sample at 06:47:57Z), so no baseline exists for latency or error-rate trends; no trend claim was made.
Why cart pod cart-74587775fc-gftlq was deleted at 06:47:36Z and replaced within the same ReplicaSet by cart-74587775fc-lvr2c (no rollout, cart Deployment revision 1) is unknown.

checkout was not confirmed affected from its own signals: a Loki query for error/fail/unavailable lines from app=checkout over 06:44:00-06:47:57Z returned no data, and the '13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout' text was observed only on frontend's client span; checkout's own logs and spans were not checked further.

The accounting Deployment runs a different image (nightly-20939609681-accounting digest sha256:51e672...) than the other 2.2.0 services; it produced no error-level log lines in 06:39:57-06:47:57Z, but its order-processing functionality was not verified.
Kubernetes events only cover 06:20:13Z-06:47:37Z, so earlier cluster history for this incident window is unavailable.
next_steps: Ask the platform owners whether valkey-cart authentication is intentional; if intended, inject the matching credential into the cart Deployment via a Secret before restarting it.
Review how requirepass/ACL users are applied to valkey-cart (chart values, Secret or an out-of-band CONFIG SET) and make that configuration declarative so client and server credentials cannot drift.
Add a cart startup dependency check that fails readiness instead of aborting the process on a Redis authentication error, and alert on valkey NOAUTH rejections.
Re-check after the fix that the cart Service has ready endpoints, that valkey errorstat_NOAUTH stops increasing, and that frontend /api/cart and /api/checkout return 200.
